socioeconomic factors are important in explaining depression prevalence, but that their relative importance differs between contexts.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the socioeconomic determinants of mental disorders are complex and need to be investigated in a multilevel manner, including the individual and the country level, and that the association of socioeconomic factors with mental health is not straightforward.
the socioeconomic factors associated with depression are different at the country and the individual level.
the individual level is more important than the contextual level in explaining cross-national differences in depression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the socioeconomic factors associated with depression are not the same as those associated with other health conditions.
the variance of depression prevalence at the country level is not explained by country-level socioeconomic factors.
individual-level socioeconomic factors are the strongest correlates of depression across countries and are the main determinants of the cross-national variation of the prevalence of depression.
